dedupe_keys.name: qnetplanner qgis plugin for network planning and gateway placement optimisation

description: QNetPlanner is a plugin for the open-source QGIS geographic information system that plans networks by choosing where to place gateways and sensors. It formulates the choice as an integer linear programme, with a greedy algorithm as a fallback when the exact solver cannot be used, and takes account of terrain, distance and cost criteria, so that planners can select a minimal or cheapest set of gateway locations covering the required sensors or users. The plugin is aimed at IoT, wireless sensor networks and infrastructure planning more broadly, framed as a facility-location and decision-support tool, and the authors say future releases will add radio-frequency simulation and more advanced decision-making. Version 1.0.0 was published in January 2026 and version 1.0.1 on 29 April 2026, for QGIS 3.22 and later, with about 900 downloads in total; the code and wiki are on GitLab. Coverage: any area mapped in QGIS. Format and access: free plugin from the official QGIS plugin repository. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): GPL-3.0-or-later. Simulation uses: optimisation of gateway and sensor placement for monitoring networks, including redundancy against node failure. Related records: GSM Cover Builder is a simpler QGIS coverage plugin, and GNI FREE plans fibre networks in QGIS.
